text.p: French stocks opened lower on Monday in a market characterised by thin volume and nervousness ahead of Thursday's civil servants' and public sector strike.
"We're still consolidating. This market is having a lot of trouble trying to get above 2,164," a trader said. "There's a little bit of nervousness ahead of Thursday's strike."
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 11.36 points or 0.53 percent at 2135.76 at 0820 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was 10.50 points lower at 2,142.
Volume was 300 million francs. Trading was expected to stay light due to the Columbus Day holiday in the United States.
Pharmaceuticals group Synthelabo was 1.8 percent higher at 448.10 francs on "good figures", traders said.
The company reported a 26.9 percent rise in first-half profit to 763.5 million francs, and said it expected a 10 percent sales rise for the full year and higher net income.
